skill.name: agent-swarm-workflow
skill.description: Multi-agent coding workflow for coordinating implementation work with NTM, Agent Mail, Beads, and BV task triage.
skill.summary: Coordinate parallel AI coding agents with prompts, task triage, reviews, and file reservations.
skill.author: Dicklesworthstone

security_audit.summary: All 65 static findings were reviewed. The backtick and command-substitution hits are Markdown examples rather than executable skill code. A semantic risk remains because the workflow tells agents to commit and push without a human approval gate.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit human approval before any commit or push, and name the target branch in the prompt.
Add scope limits for each agent before review or repair work begins, including allowed paths and bead IDs.

remediation.issue: Command examples may be mistaken for automatic actions
remediation.suggestion: Label NTM and BV commands as manual examples that should run only in the intended project environment.

semantic_findings.title: Autonomous Repository Push Instruction
semantic_findings.description: The workflow tells agents to commit all changed files and push without requiring an explicit human approval step. This can publish unintended changes or use existing git credentials in automated agent sessions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited prompt directly instructs agents to commit changed files and push. The file does not include a required human confirmation gate before that action.

content.value_statement: Parallel AI coding can become hard to coordinate across tasks, files, and reviews. This skill provides prompts and tool steps for NTM, Agent Mail, Beads, and BV.
actual_capabilities: Defines prerequisites for running a coordinated multi-agent implementation workflow.
Provides launch prompts for agents that use AGENTS.md, Agent Mail, Beads, and BV.
Explains file reservation and message patterns for reducing edit conflicts.
Lists BV commands for selecting ready tasks and checking task graph health.
Includes review prompts for self-review, cross-agent review, and UI review loops.
limitations: Requires NTM, Agent Mail, Beads, and BV to be available in the project environment.
Assumes a detailed plan and prepared beads already exist before execution starts.
Does not provide executable tooling or validate that local commands are installed.
Commit and push prompts require human review before use in shared repositories.

use_cases.title: Run Parallel Feature Work
use_cases.description: Coordinate several AI agents across prepared beads while reducing file conflicts and duplicate work.

use_cases.title: Maintain Review Momentum
use_cases.description: Use repeatable prompts for self-review, cross-review, and follow-up work after each task completes.

use_cases.title: Standardize Agent Coordination
use_cases.description: Give teams a shared workflow for task selection, status updates, and file reservations.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Small Swarm
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a prepared project
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-swarm-workflow to start three coding agents for my prepared bead plan. Include prerequisites and the initial marching orders.

prompt_templates.title: Move Agents Forward
prompt_templates.scenario: Keep work progressing after one task finishes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-swarm-workflow to create a follow-up prompt that tells agents how to select the next ready bead and report status.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Reviews
prompt_templates.scenario: Run quality checks across completed work
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-swarm-workflow to organize self-review and cross-agent review rounds for a multi-agent coding session.

prompt_templates.title: Operate a Full Implementation Cycle
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for a large project
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-swarm-workflow to plan the full execution loop from swarm launch through review, task selection, and controlled commit preparation.

output_examples.input: Start a four-agent implementation session for a project with prepared beads.
output_examples.output: A launch checklist, initial agent instructions, Agent Mail coordination steps, and task selection guidance for BV.

output_examples.input: Help agents continue after finishing one bead.
output_examples.output: A concise follow-up prompt that refreshes project context, checks messages, selects a ready bead, and announces the next task.

output_examples.input: Set up quality review after several agents have changed code.
output_examples.output: A review sequence that covers self-review, cross-agent review, broad code exploration, and test coverage checks.

best_practices: Prepare the plan, beads, AGENTS.md, and coordination tools before starting agents.
Reserve files before editing and announce active work with bead IDs.
Require human approval before commits, pushes, or broad repository changes.
anti_patterns: Starting agents before tasks and dependencies are clearly defined.
Letting agents edit the same files without reservations or status messages.
Running commit or push prompts without reviewing the final diff first.

faq.question: What does this skill coordinate?
faq.answer: It coordinates AI coding agents using prepared tasks, shared prompts, Agent Mail messages, file reservations, and BV task triage.

faq.question: Does it create the project plan?
faq.answer: No. It assumes a plan and polished beads already exist before the execution workflow begins.

faq.question: Which tools does it reference?
faq.answer: It references NTM for sessions, Agent Mail for coordination, Beads for tasks, and BV for task selection.

faq.question: Can it prevent all merge conflicts?
faq.answer: No. It provides reservation and communication patterns, but teams must still review changes and resolve conflicts.

faq.question: Is this only for Claude Code?
faq.answer: No. The workflow mentions Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini-style agents, but the report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code support.

faq.question: Should agents push changes automatically?
faq.answer: No. Treat commit and push prompts as requiring explicit human approval and a reviewed diff.
